correctness.rationale: Write X,Y with first-superdiagonal coordinates a,b,c and A,B,C. If b or B nonzero the remaining equations give XY=0. Otherwise XY=tE14 and square-zero plus commutation is exactly P Q=t[[0,1],[1,0]], P=[[a,d],[A,D]], Q=[[e,E],[c,C]]. For t!=0 P is invertible, Q uniquely determined and f,F free, proving GL_2×A². Stable complete flags on the regular k[s,t]/(s²,t²) module are indexed by P¹(k), giving q+1 Borel orbits of size |B4|/|H×|=q³(q−1)³. q=2 and q=3 independent coordinate enumerations reproduce 24 nonzero pairs at q2 and 2 fibers of 432 each at q3. Finite tests do not prove general fields.
